final.title: Tool use before automation: choose one workflow first
final.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not tied it to a real workflow yet, the first question is not “which AI tool?” It is: which repeatable job should we look at first?

Pick one workflow that happens every week and has a clear output: customer replies, invoice data entry, lead qualification, or something similar. Then map it on paper before you automate anything.

Write down three things: what enters the workflow, where the manual steps happen, and what decision rule is being used. If the work depends on your judgment, or your approval is the control gate, say that plainly. That is not a failure; it is the boundary. Human approval stays in place for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

For small businesses, the next decision is often whether the problem is tool use or AI. If your email, CRM, documents, and other SaaS tools are not connected yet, integration is usually the cheaper thing to test first. AI is better kept for repeatable patterns and rule-based decisions, not exceptions or one-off judgment calls.

So the practical next step is simple: choose one workflow, document the handoffs, and mark the approval point. If the process is still mostly manual after that, you have a bounded problem worth reviewing. If the process is already well connected, then AI may have a sensible place. The tricky part is usually not the model; it is the plumbing.
